skill.name: marp-slide
skill.description: Create polished Marp presentation decks from topics, outlines, or rough notes. The skill provides seven themes, embedded CSS templates, image layout patterns, and slide quality guidance.
skill.summary: Create themed Marp Markdown slide decks with reusable templates and presentation design guidance.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, CSS border values, official documentation links, and a GitHub Actions example. Confirmed risk is limited to low-risk Google Fonts imports in theme CSS, plus a medium semantic issue where local file rendering is recommended without trust-boundary warnings.

remediation.issue: Remote font imports in bundled themes
remediation.suggestion: Use system font stacks, bundle approved fonts, or clearly document that rendering may contact Google Fonts.

remediation.issue: Local file access guidance lacks a trust warning
remediation.suggestion: State that --allow-local-files should only be used for trusted decks and reviewed local asset paths.

semantic_findings.description: The advanced features guide recommends Marp rendering with local file access but does not warn users to restrict this to trusted decks and assets. content.value_statement: Presentation drafts often need structure, theme choices, and Marp-specific syntax. This skill turns topics or rough notes into styled Marp decks with reusable themes.
actual_capabilities: Creates Marp Markdown decks from topics, outlines, or rough notes.
Selects among seven built-in themes for business, technical, academic, creative, and general decks.
Applies Marp frontmatter, slide separators, lead slides, pagination, and image syntax.
Uses embedded CSS templates for decks that are ready for Marp CLI or the VS Code extension.
Adds side, centered, full-background, and multi-image layouts using documented Marpit patterns.
Improves vague requests by tightening headings, bullet counts, whitespace, and visual hierarchy.
limitations: It produces Markdown slide files, not final PDFs or PPTX exports by itself.
It depends on Marp tools for rendering and export.
Remote font imports in bundled CSS may contact Google Fonts during rendering.
It cannot verify image licensing or factual accuracy without user-provided sources.

use_cases.title: Build Lecture Slides
use_cases.description: Turn lesson topics into clean Marp slides with concise headings, bullets, and optional diagrams.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Talks
use_cases.description: Create code-friendly decks with dark or tech themes, structured sections, and image placement patterns.

use_cases.title: Draft Business Presentations
use_cases.description: Convert plans, reports, or proposals into professional slides with formal styling and table support.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Marp slide deck about [topic] for [audience]. Use a clear theme and make 6 to 8 slides.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this outline into a professional Marp deck. Choose a suitable theme, improve the flow, and keep each slide concise: [outline]

prompt_templates.title: Add Visual Layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Marp slides for [topic] using the [theme] style. Include image placement suggestions for these assets: [image list].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workshop Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with structure and constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Marp workshop deck for [session title]. Include sections, exercises, summary slides, speaker-friendly pacing, and a polished technical theme.

output_examples.input: Create slides about cloud computing basics for new engineers.
output: A default-themed Marp deck with a title slide, concept slides, benefits, risks, and a summary.
Headings are concise, each slide has focused bullets, and the file is ready for Marp rendering.

output_examples.input: Make my Python tutorial slides look cool.
output: A tech-themed deck with a dark background, code-friendly typography, and clear section breaks.
Dense tutorial notes are split into shorter slides with consistent visual hierarchy.

output_examples.input: Create a Q1 business review presentation from these notes.
output: A business-themed deck with formal tone, table-ready styling, and a logical report flow.
The presentation includes an overview, metrics, analysis, next steps, and closing slide.

best_practices: Provide the audience, goal, topic scope, and desired tone before asking for a deck.
Review generated slides for factual accuracy, image rights, and sensitive information before sharing.
Render the Markdown with Marp locally and check spacing, fonts, and image paths before presenting.
anti_patterns: Do not paste large unstructured documents and expect a polished deck without guidance.
Do not use remote images or fonts in confidential presentations without approval.
Do not enable local file access for untrusted Markdown or unreviewed image paths.

faq.question: Does this skill export PDF or PPTX files?
faq.answer: No. It creates Marp Markdown that can be exported by Marp CLI or compatible editor extensions.

faq.question: Can it run in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How many themes are included?
faq.answer: It includes default, minimal, colorful, dark, gradient, tech, and business themes.

faq.question: Can I customize the generated slides?
faq.answer: Yes. The output is Markdown with embedded CSS, so you can edit content and styles directly.

faq.question: Does the skill require internet access?
faq.answer: The skill files do not require internet access, but bundled theme CSS may load Google Fonts during rendering.

faq.question: Can it improve rough notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can restructure rough notes into concise slides with a consistent theme and visual hierarchy.
